🧠 Crypto News Brief: Soft US jobs data briefly lifted Bitcoin to $87K before gains faded, while security scares, an L2 shutdown and layoffs underline a cautious market mood. Fights over crypto bank charters add to the uncertainty. 📉 Bitcoin Gives Back Jobs-Report Spike After Touching $87K US employers added just 29,000 jobs in September against roughly 90,000 expected, and unemployment rose to 4.2%. The miss briefly pushed Bitcoin above $87,000 as traders priced out an October rate hike, but the rally faded within hours, with BTC shedding about $2,000 as bond yields reversed. Bitcoin was trading near $84,600 on Saturday morning. Read full story ⚖️ Community Banks Sue OCC Over Crypto Trust Charters The Independent Community Bankers of America filed suit Friday in federal court in Washington, D.C., arguing the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency overstepped its congressional mandate by granting crypto firms limited national trust bank charters. The group says the charters give crypto companies the credibility of a bank without matching safeguards, although they do not permit taking deposits or making loans. More details 🚫 US Treasury Sanctions Hamas Network That Moved Funds via Crypto OFAC designated a Gaza-based member of Hamas's military wing, two France-based fundraisers and their two charities, Association Baraka and Ensemble C Mieux. Treasury says the network raised more than $2 million for Hamas between 2020 and 2026, sending hundreds of thousands of dollars in cryptocurrency to its Gaza contact, who also relied on money services businesses to move the funds. Caption:

**Welcome back!** It's recap day, with this week's five biggest stories and five tools to try this weekend. ChatGPT read a letter nobody could crack for 217 years, and Google's new model caught up with it. OpenAI also launched 20+ things in the middle of a rough safety week, while Anthropic lined up what could be the biggest IPO ever.

**In today's Generative AI Newsletter:**

* **ChatGPT:** What did Napoleon's secret letter say?

* **Google:** Did Gemini 4 really catch up with ChatGPT?

* **OpenAI:** What went wrong after its agents escaped?

* **ChatGPT Pro:** Why does $200 get you half as much now?

* **Anthropic:** How do you lose $42 billion and still ask for $2 trillion?


----------







----------
## ChatGPT cracked a 217-year-old secret letter

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/9cc813f5-ff58-42d9-a15c-cee01cef2549/Oct_1_-_3.jpg?t=1790843459)
Caption: 

For 217 years, a coded letter to one of Napoleon's generals sat on the list of ciphers nobody could read. OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra [cracked it in about six hours](https://carter.church/writeups/the-letter-to-marmont/).

Carter Church, an AI engineer who says he'd never broken a cipher before, gave it one scanned page from a 1969 French army journal.

* It read all 1,300 handwritten symbols straight off the image.

* A partial key already covered about a third of the letter, and Astra worked out the other two-thirds.

The letter is from March 1809, two weeks before Austria invaded Bavaria. It tells General Marmont where every army stood and not to be scared of a few troops or a gathering of rabble.

Church says the man who keeps a long-running catalog of unsolved ciphers has now marked it solved. Five symbols are still uncertain, but they don't change what it says.


----------







----------
## Google's Gemini 4 caught up with ChatGPT

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/45080403-7e67-46cc-90f0-b8014ce4a061/Oct_1_-_1.jpg?t=1790843328)
Caption: 

Google [announced Gemini 4 Argon](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/gemini-4-argon/), its first new flagship model in almost a year. Artificial Analysis, the independent benchmark site, gave it 53, the same as GPT-6 Astra. Claude Opus 5.5 still leads at 58.

It costs a fifth of Astra's price, and on one test it made things up 15% of the time versus Astra's 51%.

🧠 Crypto News Brief: Soft US jobs data and fading Fed-hike bets lifted Bitcoin toward $87K, while regulators in Washington and Brussels advanced crypto rulebooks and institutions from Tokyo to Tether pushed deeper into on-chain finance. 📊 Weak US Jobs Report Lifts Bitcoin Toward $87K The US added just 29,000 jobs in September, far below the roughly 90,000 economists expected, while unemployment ticked up to 4.2% and August was revised down to 133,000. Bitcoin held its gains and traded just under $87,000 as markets slashed the odds of an October Fed hike to about 13%. Derivatives traders had already piled in: open interest climbed by roughly $2.3 billion since Sept. 30, and perpetual funding rates rose from about 3% to 10%. Read full story → 🏛️ SEC Proposes Crypto Custody Rules as Peirce Exits The Securities and Exchange Commission proposed a dedicated custody framework for registered investment advisers and regulated funds holding crypto. Advisers could act as custodians themselves in limited cases, such as when no permitted custodian exists for an asset, and state-chartered trust companies would qualify as custodians. Chair Paul Atkins said the plan creates a compliant pathway where none existed. A 60-day comment period opens after Federal Register publication. The proposal lands as Commissioner Hester Peirce, architect of the Crypto Task Force, departs on Friday, leaving the SEC with only two commissioners. More details → 🇸🇻 IMF Waives El Salvador's Bitcoin Breach, Releases $139M The IMF board completed the second and third reviews of El Salvador's $1.4 billion loan program and released roughly $139 million, granting a waiver even though the country breached its limit on Bitcoin accumulation. The Fund accepted documentation that the extra coins came from private donations rather than public money, but said no further accumulation is envisaged beyond documented gifts. The program also requires a smaller state role in the Chivo wallet, now majority-controlled by a private operator. Read more → 💵 Tether's USDT Is Coming Home to Bitcoin Tether's USDT, which first launched on Bitcoin's Omni Layer in 2014 before migrating to Ethereum and Tron, is set to return to Bitcoin this month.
